record.what_it_does: QuickBooks Online is Intuit's cloud accounting software, and its Accounting API lets apps read and write a connected company's accounting data (customers, invoices, bills, payments, reports, etc.) on the user's behalf.
record.auth_notes: Intuit's own SDKs/docs only document OAuth 2.0 authorization-code flow for the Accounting API; there is no separate API-key or basic-auth mode for calling the API itself (Basic auth is used only for the client_id/client_secret token-exchange step within the OAuth flow). Access tokens last 60 min, refresh tokens roll for up to 100 days.
record.access_notes: A developer can sign up free and get Development (sandbox) Client ID/Secret immediately to build and test. To get Production credentials (real customer data), the app must pass Intuit's App Assessment Questionnaire/compliance review before the 'Show Credentials' option is even revealed.
record.main_blocker: Production API credentials require passing Intuit's App Assessment Questionnaire/compliance review

evidence.quote: Use the OAuth 2.0 protocol to implement authentication and authorization.
Pass the access_token value in the Authorization header of requests each time your app calls an API.
The Show Credentials switch appears only after the App Assessment Questionnaire is approved.
If you're implementing authorization for testing with a sandbox company, go to the Development section and select Keys & OAuth
uses both the REST framework, with standard HTTP methods and JSON for input and output, and GraphQL
This MCP server provides complete QuickBooks Online API integration for Claude Code and other MCP-compatible clients.
Use webhooks to receive event-triggered callbacks for entities that your app needs to stay on top of.

record.open_questions: The MCP server lives under Intuit's official GitHub org (github.com/intuit) and was announced on Intuit's own Medium dev blog as an 'early preview,' but its README oddly credits itself as 'Based on Intuit's QuickBooks Online MCP Server' (self-referential) — worth double-checking it isn't a community fork misattributed to the org. Intuit also appears to run a separate hosted MCP endpoint (mcp.quickbooks.intuit.com) in a partner-only pilot (per github.com/IntuitDeveloper/intuit-3p-ai-pilot), whose general availability status is unclear.
